definition: The chart showing all the elements in the universe, arranged in order of atomic number in groups (columns) and periods (rows); first presented in its modern form in 1869 by Mendeleev.
msAccepts: arrangement of elements in order of atomic number
columns are groups, rows are periods

definition: A vertical column of the Periodic Table; numbered 1-7 then 0 at this level, with the transition metals not usually included in the numbering.
msAccepts: vertical column of the Periodic Table
elements with the same number of outer-shell electrons

definition: A horizontal row of the Periodic Table; the period number gives the number of occupied shells (or the highest occupied shell) in the atoms of its elements.
msAccepts: horizontal row of the Periodic Table
period number = number of occupied shells

definition: An element of the middle block of the Periodic Table (shown in orange in the book's Figure 4.1); not usually included in the group numbering at this level.
msAccepts: element in the middle block of the Periodic Table
msAvoids: any metal in a numbered group

definition: A Group 1 element (lithium, sodium, potassium and the rest); reacts vigorously with water to form hydrogen and an hydroxide.
msAccepts: metal that reacts with water forming hydroxide + hydrogen
msAvoids: hydrogen (it is not a Group 1 metal)

definition: A Group 7 element (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine); reacts with hydrogen to form hydrides of similar formula (HF, HCl, HBr).
A Group 0 element (helium, neon, argon and the rest); almost completely unreactive because its outer shell is full (8 electrons, or 2 for helium).
msAccepts: unreactive because outer shell is full
msAvoids: unreactive because it has no electrons

definition: An element of the first detached row at the bottom of the Periodic Table; not actually rare despite the old name 'rare earth metals', and important in modern technology.
msAccepts: element of the first bottom row of the Periodic Table

definition: An element of the second detached row at the bottom of the Periodic Table; most are unstable and undergo radioactive decay.
msAccepts: element of the second bottom row of the Periodic Table

definition: The number of protons in the nuclei of an element's atoms; always the smaller of the two numbers printed against a symbol in the Periodic Table.
msAccepts: number of protons in the nucleus
the smaller number on the Periodic Table
msAvoids: the larger number on the chart

definition: The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom; on Periodic Tables that print isotope masses, it is the mass number of the most common isotope.
msAvoids: a weighted average of isotopes (that is Aᵣ)

definition: The weighted average mass of an element's isotopes; the number the Periodic Table shows instead of a mass number when it is not a whole number (chlorine 35.5).
msAccepts: Aᵣ as printed on the chart
msAvoids: mass of one atom of the element

definition: An energy level around the nucleus that electrons occupy; lower (inner) shells fill first, and at this level the capacities are 2, 8, then 8.
msAccepts: fills inner-before-outer, capacities 2/8/8 at this level
msAvoids: the path an electron orbits along

definition: The arrangement of electrons in an atom's shells, written with commas (chlorine 2, 8, 7); the electrons must add up to the atomic number.
The highest occupied shell of an atom; its electron count is the group number (Groups 1-7) and governs how the element reacts.
msAccepts: its electrons are the ones involved in reactions
msAvoids: the largest shell the atom could ever have

definition: Combining power; the historical reason Group 0 was numbered 0 - the noble gases were first believed to combine with nothing, hence zero combining power.
msAccepts: why the noble-gas group is numbered 0

definition: A metal oxide that reacts with acids to form salts; if soluble in water it dissolves to form an alkali (sodium oxide + water -> sodium hydroxide solution).
msAccepts: oxide reacting with acids to form salts
soluble one gives an alkali in water
msAvoids: any oxide of a metal regardless of behaviour (Al2O3 is amphoteric)

definition: A non-metal oxide that reacts with bases/alkalis to form salts; if soluble in water it dissolves to form an acidic solution (sulfur(IV) oxide + water -> sulfurous acid).
msAccepts: oxide reacting with bases/alkalis to form salts
soluble one gives an acid in water
msAvoids: any oxide of a non-metal regardless of behaviour (CO is neutral)

definition: An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases, behaving like a basic oxide and an acidic oxide at once; the book's example is aluminium oxide (Al2O3).
msAccepts: oxide reacting with both acids and bases
msAvoids: an oxide that reacts with neither

definition: An electron not tied to any one atom, free to move through the metal; its presence is why metals conduct electricity (full explanation in Chapter 9).
msAvoids: an electron shared between two named atoms

definition: A form of carbon; the book's named exception among non-metals, since it conducts electricity even though non-metals do not generally conduct.
Can be hammered into shape - a typical metal property (the adjective pairs with ductile, which means drawn into wires).
msAvoids: can be drawn into wires (that is ductile)

definition: Can be drawn into wires - a typical metal property (pairs with malleable, which means hammered into shape).
msAvoids: can be hammered into shape (that is malleable)

definition: The shine of a metal, seen when it is polished or freshly cut; not by itself proof of metal-hood (shiny sulfur crystals are still non-metal).
msAccepts: metal's shine when polished or freshly cut
msAvoids: proof that a substance is a metal
